title: Recursion Budget
statement: Implement `solve(n, limit)`. A countdown wants to make `n` recursive calls. The interpreter will allow at most `limit` of them. Return how many calls actually run: the smaller of `n` and `limit` when both are positive, otherwise 0.
constraints: A non-positive budget or countdown runs nothing
hints: If either input is less than 1, return 0.
Otherwise return the minimum of the two numbers.
Do not recurse in your solution. The budget is a closed form.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: A recursive countdown of n needs n frames before it hits the base case.

editorial: A recursive countdown of n needs n frames before it hits the base case. The useful question before you raise the recursion limit is how many of those frames the current budget still allows. min(n, limit) is that number when both are positive.
